To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
XELOX is the most cost-effective first-line chemotherapy regimen for MCRC in Japan.
the mean out-of-patient payments for 16 cycles of first-line Xelox and Xelox plus bevacizumbab for middle-income patients less than 70 years old were JPY 3,28,000 and JYP 3,76,000, respectively.

the mean out-of- pocket payment for middle-income patients < 70 years of aged was JPY 328 000 for XE-LOX and JYPY 376 000 for XEL- OX + beva, and that the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of XELO- X + bevacizumab was JPY 430 000/PFS-year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the out-of-pocket perspective of patients with MCRC.
the perspective of patients and their families.
patients' preferences, and the results may be useful for the decision-making process for patients with MCRC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
XELOX is cost-effective and XELOOX plus bevacizumb is highly cost-effective from the perspective of MCRC patients.
the incremental out-of-pocket cost of adding bevacizumabb to first-line XELOS is not cost-effective from the perspective of MCRC patients.
the cost-effectiveness of first-line XELLOX plus beavacizumab from a society or healthcare payer’s perspective is still controversial in Japan.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XELOX or XELOOX plus bevacizumbab is a cost-effective treatment option from the perspective of MCRC patients.
the out-of-pocket payments and cost-effectiveness for first-line chemotherapy are not so high in Japan.
the cost-effectiveness of bevacizumabin addition to XELOX from the perspective of MCRC patients is not high, and it is not a good idea for MCRC patients to pay for it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incremental cost-effectiveness of bevacizumabbased chemotherapy for MCRC patients is not very high, but it may be acceptable to patients.

the cost-effectiveness of first-line bevacuzimab therapy should be assessed from the perspective of payers, and the cost-effectiveness analysis of bevacizumabb should be updated with the latest clinical evidence.
the incremental cost-effectiveness of first-line chemotherapy for MCRC patients is very high.
